findings.title: Persist the post-lock guard acceptance time in every progress event
findings.body: prepare_planning_progress reads the authoritative post-attempt-lock clock_timestamp into now but never persists that guard acceptance time in the RecordSnapshot/AdvanceAttempt S03 event. idempotent_outcome inserts no event typed_payload or acceptance timestamp; S03 recorded_at instead defaults to transaction_timestamp(), before a lock wait. RecordSnapshot source_cutoff is capture time, and AdvanceAttempt started_at remains the first-stage start for subsequent transitions, so neither supplies the required per-operation event acceptance time. Frozen DOC-DB-V0.2 section 4.3 explicitly requires guard acceptance time to be recorded in the event. The committed concurrent AdvanceAttempt evidence shows event 2c992c88-47ba-4291-81dd-a7c11eb54308 recorded_at=2026-10-01T07:02:00.542133+00:00 and payload={}, while actual attempt started_at=2026-10-01T07:02:00.549403+00:00. This leaves an audit timestamp earlier than the authority check despite correctly enforcing the current lease/deadline.
findings.requested_change: Store the exact server-derived post-lock accepted time in coordination context and persist it atomically in each internal progress event without changing public owner/wire descriptors or accepting caller time. Add real PostgreSQL assertions for both owners, including a successful bounded lock wait and historical replay preserving the original timestamp.
